subject: Clarify: derivative-modeling assurances and retention exceptions
messages:

Subject: Clarification needed: model training and retention edge cases

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week — HelixPay is excited about Redwood's latency profile. Before we proceed to a pilot, our security and legal teams have two specific asks we need to confirm in writing: 1) that Redwood does not use customer content to train or improve models (including derivative-modeling/weight updates), and 2) a clear explanation of any retention exceptions (e.g., debug snapshots, backups, legal holds) that might persist beyond the standard deletion window.

Attached is our short FedReg questionnaire; we filled relevant sections but left some items blank where we need your language. Could you reply with a concise statement we can include in our risk assessment, plus any operational notes (typical retention TTLs and the main exceptions)?

Appreciate a quick turnaround — our procurement deadline is July 25.

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Product Security
HelixPay

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Clarification needed: model training and retention edge cases

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear asks and the questionnaire. Below is language you can paste into your assessment, followed by operational details and a short list of exceptions.

Short assurance for contract/policy: 
"Redwood Inference does not use customer-provided inference input or uploaded customer data to train, fine-tune, or perform derivative model training on Redwood-hosted public models. Customer content is not incorporated into model weights or downstream model training pipelines unless the customer explicitly opts in via a documented data-sharing agreement. For Dedicated and Private deployments, model training is only performed under explicit customer authorization and separate contractual terms."

Operational retention summary (typical/default):
- Primary inference request payloads: retained transiently in memory and ephemeral caches; not persisted to long-term training stores.
- Request logs/telemetry: stored for 30 days by default for billing/operational analytics; can be configured shorter for enterprise contracts.
- Debug snapshots & crash dumps: retained up to 90 days by default for postmortem/rollback; deleted earlier upon request unless subject to legal hold.
- Backups & snapshots (infrastructure level): rotated on a 30–90 day schedule depending on deployment type; snapshots containing tenant metadata are purged according to the retention policy tied to the deployment.

Notable exceptions and nuance:
1) Legal/compliance holds: data subject to subpoena or regulatory hold will be preserved until released by the custodian.
2) Customer-requested audit packages: if HelixPay requests a security/evidence package (logs, traces), Redwood will produce and temporarily retain those artifacts as agreed in the SOW.
3) Operational backups in Dedicated deployments: customers can choose snapshot retention windows; default window may be longer than hosted API unless contractually changed.
4) Telemetry-derived aggregations: aggregated, de-identified metrics (e.g., system performance histograms) are used to improve the platform but do not contain customer-specific content for model training.

Attachments: I attached an internal ops checklist that maps the lifecycle for each artifact type and TTLs. If you want a legally-worded contract clause, Marissa can propose SOW language.

Cheers,
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Adding a couple operational specifics from infra that help explain the "why" and mitigations we offer: 

- KV cache & ephemeral prefix caches: never written to persistent training datasets. These are memory-backed or local ephemeral disks and are evicted based on LRU and TTL. Customers on Dedicated can opt for additional isolation (per-tenant volumes cleared on decommission).
- Debug snapshots: these are minimized to metadata + anonymized traces by default. Full-text snapshots are only captured when explicitly enabled for a troubleshooting engagement; those are tagged and have fast-path deletion once the debug ticket closes (SUP-8721).
- Snapshots & backups: for hosted customers, infrastructure snapshots are tenant-scoped but do include encrypted metadata. We support a 30-day default retention; enterprise customers can request shorter windows or attestations for deletion.
- Proof of deletion: we provide a tombstone + wipe confirmation workflow; for critical customers we can deliver a signed deletion note via DocuSign.

If HelixPay needs contractual language referencing these behaviors, recommend we propose: 
1) a non-training warranty clause (as Priyom wrote), and 
2) an appendix listing artifact classes, default TTLs, and exception paths (legal hold, customer-requested audit, troubleshooting with explicit opt-in).

Mina
Infra Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
